queries.known_fail_reason: Engine nearness returns -20 when path == near (engine/src/server.rs:837-846), so the file the caller passes as `near` is demoted to last. Measured: [test/client.test.ts, test/client-features.test.ts, src/client.ts].
queries.note: The primary defect this lane must expose: `near` currently cannot mean 'rank the file I am editing first'.

queries.measurement: The pair RS03/RS04 is the proximity test: identical query, only `near` moves. Require (a) the two result orders differ, (b) the same-folder peer of `near` is rank 1 in both, (c) the near file itself is not rank 1 in either until the -20 rule is revisited.
queries.note: Measured (near=test/client.test.ts): [test/client-features.test.ts, src/client.ts, test/client.test.ts].

queries.call: search("readme", in=<root>, limit=10) after {op:"open"} of <root>/README.md >=30s earlier
queries.measurement: Paired: run the query once before any open (control) and once >=30s after an open of README.md. Accept the frecency claim only if the paired rank delta of README.md is >= 1 with a CI excluding 0 over >=10 alternated rounds. A single open followed by a single query is not evidence.
queries.note: Not measured by the advisor probe (precondition costs 30s and is stateful).

queries.call: search("client", in=<root>, limit=10, boost=true) vs boost=false
queries.measurement: boost = frecency + git history + mtime. On the archive corpus (no .git, uniform mtimes) both arms measured byte-identical output - a structurally degenerate test. Run it on a git-initialised corpus or the live worktree; a tie is a valid result and must disable the default.
queries.note: Measured identical: [src/client.ts, test/client.test.ts, test/client-features.test.ts] for both arms.

queries.call: search("client", in=<root>, limit=10, git="modified") after touching a known file
queries.note: The archive corpus has no .git, so this query is currently unmeasurable; it is listed to make the corpus requirement explicit, not to score. The touched file is chosen by the scorer so the expectation is computed, not hardcoded.

queries.call: search("client", in=<root>, limit=10) - inspect result text for reason tags
queries.measurement: Accept #42 only when each returned row carries a reason tag ([exact], [glob], [git:modified], [proximity], or an engine-computed score component) AND the tag is consistent with the ordering (a row tagged [exact] must not be outranked by a row with no reason). Tags alone are not acceptance evidence.
queries.note: Non-gating until #42 ships.

acceptance.pointer: bench/judgments/wave2-bars.json - per-lane floors, claim gates and latency budgets
non_negotiables: A wave2 baseline run of THIS file on the corpus above must be committed before any ranking claim (pre-registration). wave2-probes.json is the advisor's provisional observation, not the baseline.
Tier-L (lane gate): zero_result_rate = 0.00 on declared-answerable must_hit queries; false_positive_rate = 0.00 on negatives; feature-gated and known_fail rows are excluded from Tier-L but reported.
Tier-C (claim gate): paired per-query delta with BCa CI excluding 0 and point delta >= +0.05 nDCG@10, and no lane regressing by > 0.02.
Never cite the corpus-meta contaminant or held-out overfitting: publish this set as a smoke set and require the verifier to run a generated/permuted variant for acceptance.

measurement_notes.gate: Wave-2 bars are corpus-relative; the whole-disk/5k-fixture latency rows stay governed by the wave-1 latency baseline (paired comparison, CI excluding 0).
